claims.text: 2nd Avenue & Cherry Street had 12 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 0 people killed.
These counts are 2nd Avenue & Cherry Street's own: the city's record places 415 of the 437 records within 100 m at another intersection or street, and they are left out.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $822,000 a year.
55% of crashes here were recorded as “angles” crashes, against 16% at the city's worst crash locations.
55% of crashes here were recorded as “entering at angle” crashes, against 16% at the city's worst crash locations.
23% of crashes here were recorded as “motor vehicle struck pedalcyclist, front end at angle” crashes, against 3% at the city's worst crash locations.

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: passed the causal gate (pedestrian injury crashes changed -33% (95% interval -52% to -13%) at 371 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing); a second run of the same design on 366 sites agrees.

Backplates with Retroreflective Borders would avoid about 0.4 crashes a year (CMF 1410, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $123,000 a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red.

Pavement Friction Management would avoid about 0.4 crashes a year (CMF 195, the only eligible record; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $129,000 a year; check on site: the pavement's friction is low now (wet-road crashes alone do not show it).
The Seattle Department of Transportation (SDOT) is responsible for 2nd Avenue, Cherry Street, James Street (no route reference, so presumed a city street).
A request letter to the Seattle Department of Transportation (SDOT) is ready to draft from these facts.

agent.summary: In Seattle, 2nd Avenue & Cherry Street had 153 injury crashes in the 5 years from 31 Oct 2021 (R6). Its crashes have in common motor vehicle struck pedalcyclist, front end at angle: 31 crashes, 7.0% vs 3.3% citywide (R2). Leading Pedestrian Interval signals were already in place here in 2009 and were measured in this city to have reduced pedestrian injury crashes by 33% at 371 sites; repeat risk here was not shown (R3). Fixes the record supports include Lighting and Pavement Friction Management (R4). The road owners that must act are SDOT (R5).
